label: <DEL> step of short (L=3-4) sequences starting with a/c/d/y
explanation: Fires only at the delimiter step (100% of mass), i.e. when the model must emit the first original token. Restricted to short sequences: L=3 (37% of mass, 27x lift) and L=4 (58%), rare at L=5, never at L>=6. Strongly modulated by the first original token (the token to be output): a (49% of mass, 25x lift), d, c (~19% each), y, b weaker; essentially silent for other first tokens. The last original token also matters (m, h, 2, o, r, x, k, e raise it); top activations look like a m h <DEL>, a a k m <DEL>. Never fires during the original or copy phases. Activation appears to be a graded combination of these factors, so boolean predicates leave precision low: phase==1 & L<=4 & first in {a,c,d} reaches recall 0.74 / mass 0.82 but precision only 0.17; adding the last-token set raises precision to ~0.33 at the cost of recall.
